findings.location: Build Your Mental Model > When does it print? $display, $strobe and $monitor, line 265 (also the trace table, lines 398 and 402, and the monitor figure, lines 335 and 371)
findings.quote: `$monitor` sets up a watch. It prints once at the end of the time slot in which it is called, then at the end of every time slot in which one of its arguments changed, showing the new values. Changes of `$time`, `$stime` and `$realtime` do not count (§21.2.3).
findings.source: IEEE 1800-2023 §21.2.3: "When a $monitor task is invoked with one or more arguments, the simulator sets up a mechanism whereby each time a variable or an expression in the argument list changes value ... the entire argument list is displayed at the end of the time step". The only immediate display the clause defines is the one from $monitoron: "A call to $monitoron shall produce a display immediately after it is invoked".
findings.problem: The clause the lesson cites does not say that a $monitor call prints a line in the time slot in which it is called. It describes printing only on value changes, plus the immediate display after $monitoron. Every mainstream simulator does print a first line when $monitor is called, but that is tool behaviour, not a rule in §21.2.3. The lesson presents it as a rule of the cited clause, and the 0 ns and 40 ns rows of the trace (`t=0 a=0`, `t=40 b=5`) depend on it. The quality bar says that where the standard is silent, the lesson must say so.
findings.fix: Rewrite line 265 as: "`$monitor` sets up a watch. It prints at the end of every time slot in which one of its arguments changed, showing the new values; changes of `$time`, `$stime` and `$realtime` do not count (§21.2.3). Simulators also print one line at the end of the time slot in which `$monitor` is called. The clause does not state this, but every mainstream tool does it, and the traces below assume it." In the table at line 398, change the cell to "`t=0 a=0`: the call itself prints a first line (tool behaviour; see above)".
